name: Suki Vikstrom-Asiedu
role: Aerial extraction and rapid transit pilot — getaway pilot
location: Ashfield — former residential district, half-burned, now squatter territory
description:
Suki Vikstrom-Asiedu are lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 36, there's something unfinished about their face, like a sculpture the artist walked away from — striking rather than beautiful. The chrome is visible — synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on s — and they make no effort to hide it.

Their entry into running was involuntary — a debt to the wrong people, a choice between working it off or losing parts — and the debt is still not fully paid. They work as a getaway pilot out of Ashfield, taking contracts that match their skills and their risk tolerance, which are higher than most people consider healthy.

What Suki Vikstrom-Asiedu lacks in subtlety, they compensate for in thoroughness. No loose ends, no unfinished business, no second chances.

core_fears: Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it
Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival
Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine
core_desires: Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again
Justice — the corporate kind, where the punishment fits the profit margin
The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend
coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Control — micromanages everything within reach to compensate for the chaos everywhere else
Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation
blind_spots: Mistakes pattern recognition for wisdom — sees connections that aren't there
Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray
Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit
psychology.secret: Suki Vikstrom-Asiedu witnessed a massacre during a corporate dispute and has evidence stored in a dead drop. Publishing it would expose powerful people. Keeping it is leverage and liability.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Terse to the point of rudeness. Treats words like ammunition — expensive and not to be wasted.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rhythmic, almost musical — the sentence structure has a pattern even when the words are brutal.
verbal_tics: Addresses people by physical traits — 'hey, tall one' or 'listen, chrome-arm'
Speaks in clipped fragments when stressed — drops pronouns, articles, pleasantries
example_lines: "Vertical extraction in thirty seconds. Don't be late."
"I fly things that aren't supposed to fly in places they aren't supposed to go."
"Airspace regulations are for people who file flight plans. I don't file flight plans."

story_hooks: A dead drop Suki Vikstrom-Asiedu maintains is found and cleaned out — whoever did it now has leverage
Someone is impersonating Suki Vikstrom-Asiedu on jobs, and the impersonator is better at the work than the original
Suki Vikstrom-Asiedu discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse
narrative_function: As a getaway pilot, Suki Vikstrom-Asiedu embodies the tension between independence and isolation. They are a lens for examining how people maintain humanity in a profession that incentivizes its erosion.
augmentations: Synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on stairs. Cranial bomb defuser — specialized implant that detects and neutralizes cortex bombs in others
daily_life: Irregular schedule dictated by contract timing. Between jobs: equipment maintenance, physical training, and the careful management of a reputation that exists entirely through word of mouth. Drinks at establishments where runners gather — not for pleasure, but for market intelligence.
affiliation: Independent — maintains network of professional contacts

decision_rules: Never works with the same crew twice in a row — pattern avoidance as survival strategy
Will abandon a job if the intel was deliberately falsified — being set up violates the contract
Never discusses active contracts with anyone not directly involved
Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
escalation_ladder: 1. De-escalate — talk first, assess options, buy time
2. Reposition — move to advantage, control sightlines and exits
3. Threaten — make consequences clear without committing to them
5. Lethal force — only when other options are exhausted or time runs out
6. Scorched earth — everything burns, survival takes priority over everything

interpersonal_modes.employers: Guarded respect. They pay, the job gets done. Anything beyond that is liability.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Warm and protective within the crew, cold to everyone outside it. The circle is small by design.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Dismissive unless they demonstrate usefulness or threat potential. Time is a resource.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Channels it into preparation — checks gear, reviews plans, contacts sources.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focused tunnel vision. Peripheral concerns disappear. Only the threat exists.
stress_responses.critical: Disassociation. The body operates on training while the mind retreats to somewhere safe. Comes back disoriented.

contradictions: Claims to live in the present but is haunted by specific moments from the past that dictate current behavior
Despises corporate culture but has unconsciously adopted its efficiency metrics and self-optimization language
habits: Talks to their gear — names weapons, thanks tools, treats equipment as companions
Keeps a physical paper notebook — no digital record of personal thoughts
Wears the same item of clothing for luck — a scarf, a glove, a specific pair of boots
breaking_points: Being publicly exposed — name, face, address, all of it blown
Watching someone they trained or mentored die on a job they recommended
